body:
### Motivation
- The rental contract pages should not display the chatbot icon according to the requested layout change. 
- The app previously showed the chatbot icon on the `/test` page only, but it could appear on rental contract pages when navigating with queries. 

### Description
- Updated `pages/_app.tsx` to compute `isRentalContractPage` from `router.asPath` and use it to hide the chatbot. 
- Changed `isChatbotVisible` to `router.pathname === '/test' && !isRentalContractPage` so `ChatBotWidget` is not shown on `rental-contract` pages. 
- No other components or styles were modified; the `ChatBotWidget` continues to receive the `visible` prop as before. 

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change. 
- A local commit was created containing the single-line logic update in `pages/_app.tsx`.

### Motivation

- Fix incorrect generated import lines which produced duplicated or path-prefixed names like `protos/.../foo.proto.proto` instead of simple `foo.proto` when writing schemas via `schemas::write_all`.
- Ensure the build-time proto generation supports generics, transparent types, and fields using `skip` and `into` attributes by exercising them in the proto build test.

### Description

- Normalize emitted import statements in `schemas::write_all` by taking the file basename and stripping a trailing `.proto` before writing `import "{name}.proto";`.
- Extend `tests/proto_build_test` with new types: `MilliSeconds`, transparent `TransparentId`, generic `Envelope<T>`, `BuildConfig` (uses `into` and `skip`), `BuildRequest`, and `BuildResponse`, and register them in `proto_imports` and RPC method signatures to exercise generation paths.
- All changes are limited to `src/lib.rs` (import normalization) and `tests/proto_build_test/src/main.rs` (test additions).

### Testing

- Ran `cargo test --all-features --no-run` to build with all features enabled and verify codegen and proc-macros compile.
- The compilation finished successfully and test binaries were produced, noting tests were not executed (only compilation was performed).

body:
# 🚗 Implement Vehicle Detail Page with Specifications and Image Gallery

## 📋 Description

This PR implements a comprehensive vehicle detail page for the AutoSelect Car Ordering Platform. The page provides customers with complete vehicle information including high-quality images, detailed specifications, features, pricing, and real-time availability status. The implementation focuses on performance, accessibility, and SEO optimization to deliver an excellent user experience across all devices.

**Task ID:** `b9a8161a-1572-49d8-ba68-78e9b67e8e9c`  
**Priority:** 🔴 High  
**Story Points:** 3

---

## ✨ What's Implemented

### Core Features
- **📸 Image Gallery**: Interactive gallery with Unsplash API integration, featuring lazy loading, zoom functionality, and thumbnail navigation
- **📑 Tabbed Interface**: Organized information sections (Overview, Features, Specifications, Pricing) with accessible navigation
- **📊 Real-time Availability**: Dynamic stock status indicator with visual feedback
- **💰 Pricing Information**: Comprehensive pricing display including MSRP, incentives, and financing options
- **🎨 Responsive Design**: Seamless experience across desktop, tablet, and mobile devices
- **🔍 SEO Optimization**: Meta tags, structured data (JSON-LD), and Open Graph integration
- **♿ Accessibility**: WCAG compliant with proper ARIA labels and keyboard navigation

### Technical Implementation
- React with TypeScript for type-safe component development
- React Query for efficient data fetching and caching
- Unsplash API integration for high-quality vehicle imagery
- React Router integration for navigation and deep linking
- Comprehensive test coverage with Jest and React Testing Library

---

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria Status

| Criteria | Status | Notes |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Vehicle detail page loads within 3 seconds | ✅ | Optimized with lazy loading and React Query caching |
| Image gallery with Unsplash API and lazy loading | ✅ | Implemented with progressive image loading |
| Tabbed sections for information organization | ✅ | Overview, Features, Specifications, Pricing tabs |
| Real-time availability indicator | ✅ | Dynamic stock status with refresh capability |
| Responsive design across all devices | ✅ | Mobile-first approach with breakpoints |
| SEO-optimized with meta tags and structured data | ✅ | JSON-LD schema and Open Graph tags |
| Configure button for customization flow | ✅ | Integrated with vehicle configuration routing |
| Accessibility compliant | ✅ | ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, semantic HTML |

---

## 🛠 Technical Approach

### Architecture
- **Component Structure**: Modular component design with clear separation of concerns
- **State Management**: React state with React Query for server state
- **API Integration**: Custom hooks for data fetching with error handling and retry logic
- **Image Optimization**: Unsplash API with responsive image sizing (1200x800 main, 400x300 thumbnails)
- **Performance**: Lazy loading, code splitting, and memoization strategies

### Key Technologies
- React 18+ with TypeScript
- React Query for data fetching
- React Router v6 for routing
- Unsplash API for vehicle imagery
- Jest & React Testing Library for testing

---

## 📁 Files Changed

### 🆕 New Files Created

#### **Services**
- `frontend/src/services/unsplash.ts` - Unsplash API integration service with caching and error handling

#### **Components**
- `frontend/src/components/VehicleDetail/VehicleDetailPage.tsx` - Main page component with SEO and navigation
- `frontend/src/components/VehicleDetail/ImageGallery.tsx` - Interactive image gallery with zoom and lazy loading
- `frontend/src/components/VehicleDetail/SpecificationTabs.tsx` - Accessible tabbed interface for information sections
- `frontend/src/components/VehicleDetail/AvailabilityIndicator.tsx` - Real-time stock status indicator
- `frontend/src/components/VehicleDetail/VehicleOverview.tsx` - Key specifications and pricing overview
- `frontend/src/components/VehicleDetail/FeaturesList.tsx` - Categorized features display
- `frontend/src/components/VehicleDetail/TechnicalSpecs.tsx` - Detailed specifications table
- `frontend/src/components/VehicleDetail/PricingSection.tsx` - Comprehensive pricing information

#### **Hooks**
- `frontend/src/hooks/useVehicleDetail.ts` - React Query hook for vehicle data fetching

#### **Utilities**
- `frontend/src/utils/seo.ts` - SEO meta tags and structured data generation

#### **Tests**
- `frontend/src/__tests__/components/VehicleDetail/ImageGallery.test.tsx` - Image gallery component tests
- `frontend/src/__tests__/components/VehicleDetail/SpecificationTabs.test.tsx` - Tabbed interface tests
- `frontend/src/__tests__/services/unsplash.test.ts` - Unsplash service tests

### ✏️ Modified Files
- `frontend/src/App.tsx` - Added vehicle detail route (`/vehicles/:id`)

---

## 🧪 Testing Instructions

### Prerequisites
```bash
npm install
```

### Running Tests
```bash
# Run all tests
npm test

# Run tests with coverage
npm test -- --coverage

# Run specific test suites
npm test ImageGallery
npm test SpecificationTabs
npm test unsplash
```

### Manual Testing

1. **Navigate to Vehicle Detail Page**
   ```
   http://localhost:3000/vehicles/[vehicle-id]
   ```

2. **Test Image Gallery**
   - Verify images load from Unsplash
   - Click thumbnails to change main image
   - Test zoom functionality
   - Verify lazy loading on scroll

3. **Test Tabbed Interface**
   - Click each tab (Overview, Features, Specifications, Pricing)
   - Test keyboard navigation (Tab, Arrow keys)
   - Verify content updates correctly

4. **Test Availability Indicator**
   - Check stock status displays correctly
   - Verify color coding (green/yellow/red)
   - Test refresh functionality

5. **Test Responsive Design**
   - Desktop (1920px, 1440px, 1024px)
   - Tablet (768px, 834px)
   - Mobile (375px, 414px)

6. **Test Accessibility**
   - Screen reader navigation
   - Keyboard-only navigation
   - Color contrast verification

7. **Test SEO**
   - View page source for meta tags
   - Verify JSON-LD structured data
   - Check Open Graph tags

### Test Coverage Goals
- Unit Tests: >80% coverage
- Component Tests: All user interactions covered
- Integration Tests: API integration and routing

---

## 🚀 Deployment Notes

### Environment Variables
Ensure the following environment variables are configured:

```env
REACT_APP_UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY=your_unsplash_access_key
REACT_APP_API_BASE_URL=your_api_base_url
```

### Build Process
```bash
# Production build
npm run build

# Verify build
npm run preview
```

### Performance Considerations
- Images are lazy-loaded to improve initial page load
- React Query caching reduces API calls
- Code splitting implemented for optimal bundle size
- Consider CDN for static assets in production

### SEO Considerations
- Ensure server-side rendering or pre-rendering for production
- Submit updated sitemap to search engines
- Verify structured data with Google Rich Results Test

---

## ⚠️ Breaking Changes

**None** - This is a new feature with no breaking changes to existing functionality.

---

## 📝 Migration Steps

**Not Applicable** - No database migrations or data transformations required.

---

## ✔️ Reviewer Checklist

### Code Quality
- [ ] Code follows project TypeScript and React conventions
- [ ] Components are properly typed with TypeScript interfaces
- [ ] No console.log or debugging code left in
- [ ] Error handling is comprehensive and user-friendly
- [ ] Loading states are handled appropriately

### Functionality
- [ ] All acceptance criteria are met
- [ ] Image gallery works smoothly with Unsplash integration
- [ ] Tabbed interface is intuitive and accessible
- [ ] Availability indicator updates correctly
- [ ] Pricing information displays accurately
- [ ] Configure button navigates correctly

### Performance
- [ ] Page loads within 3 seconds
- [ ] Images are lazy-loaded
- [ ] No unnecessary re-renders
- [ ] React Query caching is properly conf

author: copilot
body:
Slash queue was being emptied when only partial deletions occurred due to quota limits. Additionally, quota tracking was client-side only, causing issues in multi-user deployments where quota is shared.

## Changes

### Slash Queue Bug Fix
- Keep remaining comments in queue when quota limits prevent full deletion
- Handle quota exceeded errors during deletion properly
- Show clear messages about remaining comments

### Server-Side Centralized Quota Management
- Real-time quota broadcasting via SSE to all connected clients
- Quota reservation system using 1000-unit chunks for fair distribution
- Track connected users and active deletion operations
- Per-minute quota tracking alongside daily limits

### Parallel Deletions
- New `deleteCommentsParallel()` method for faster bulk deletion
- Configurable parallel count via `MAX_PARALLEL_DELETIONS` (default: 5)
- UI updates in real-time as each deletion completes

### New Environment Variables
```
YOUTUBE_DAILY_QUOTA_LIMIT=10000
YOUTUBE_PER_MINUTE_QUOTA_LIMIT=1800000
QUOTA_RESERVATION_CHUNK_SIZE=1000
MAX_PARALLEL_DELETIONS=5
```

### UI Updates
QuotaProgressBar now displays reserved quota, connected users count, and shared quota notification.

![Quota Panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ab7d09b-740f-4a74-990b-8ab3e599928b)

## Key Files
- `src/lib/server/quota.ts` - Reservation system and SSE broadcasting
- `src/routes/api/quota/stream/+server.ts` - SSE endpoint
- `src/lib/stores/quota.ts` - Client-side SSE connection and reservation methods
- `src/lib/services/youtube.ts` - Parallel deletion support

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

We made the slash queue be persisted however there seems to be a bug when only partial amounts of them can be delete. I had 7 comments in the queue, and the quota allowed for only 5 of them to be deleted. When the 5 were deleted, even though there was a message shown that the remaining comments will stay in the queue - the queue cot reset and refreshed and it became completely empty. I think we reset the queue when its contents get deleted, but it seems we didn't account for the case that not all of its contents get deleted. There could be errors on delete, but also the quota might fill up while deleting - so we need to accoutn for those cases and not just empty the queue. please check and fix
- we need to make sure our app is able to handle parallel use. meaning if 5 different people use our app, all of them shoul dbe able to use the app. now technically this probably works fine, because most code and logik runs on the browser anyway, however the quota calculation and keeping track on it needs to happen on the server centrally, so the current quota is reflected for all users in realtime.

meaning that if person b uses up 2000 Quota points, all other users should have their quota indicator be updated - so the deletions etc can account for this.

We can implement certain mechanisms to have the best user experience while also have the best tracking accuracy and api efficiency usage - for example if a user starts to delete comments, the ammount of quota usage could be taken into account by the server already. So we could have the quota indicator show what quota was already used, what quota is `reserved` (meaning a user started the deletion pogress and that quota will be used up IF the deletion completely runs through and succeeds! - so a secondary check how much quota actually was used up is also needed - reserved - actual usage. If there is a difference, meaning if less comments were deleted than planned, than the actual used up quota would be calulated accurately that way.)
Via this we can also implement fair-use quotas. Meaning tepending on current users, we can prevent certain users to straight up uing up all of the quota themselves. This could be calculated smartly also in a user friendly way via hom many users are online and connected via google (meaning they can atually delete comments), how much time is left until quota resets and how much quota is left.

Of course we want to allow users to delete as much as they need, we don't want to be hellbent on reserving usage - 
I think a good idea could be, that the reservation calculation and fair use allowance happens on the fly.

So we could make it so the reservation is overbookable by multiple people. Example:
- 10000 quota left
- person A wants to delete comments that would cost 7000 Quota and they start the deletion process - server books the 7000 reservation internally - but the system communicates and shows realtime reservations in 1000 Quota units steps. So the client tells the server that the total quota usage will be 7000, but they reserve 1000 and start the deletion of the comments. The server communicates this reservation to all clients, so they can take the new quota amount into account. After the 1000 quota unit comments are deleted, the clients communicates with the server if it can proceed with the next 1000 units of quota usage - so the server reserves the next 1000 Units package and confirm continuation to client who continues with the delete and so on
- if person B now comes in and wants to delete 5000 units work of comments, he will also communicate with the server that he wants to use up 5000 units. The server now knows that the quota will not be enough to satisfy all clients, but allows the person B to use the available quota also in 1000 Steps. Once the quota fills up, the server will deny further requests saying the quota is full, and the client will have to wait for the reset timer , and the vlients of course perfectly handle this case and update their users that the remaining comments couldn't be deleted because the quota is full for the day, adn that they can continue after the reset timer runs out.

I know this sounds complicated, but I think this will allow for the full quota to be able to be used in full at all times but also as fairly distributed as possible - with the users beig able to see that the service is currently being used by others as well. Maybe we can extend the quota viewer with also the amount of logged in users being shown and broadcasted to all clients (only the number of currently logged in users - logged in users mean those who are connected to youtube and can use quota) - so users themselves can see and understand why the quota gets used up even if they are not the one causing its use.

For this reason of course the server needs to be able to handle reads and writes in parallel and keep the quota and all clients accurately updated at all times. So please make sure the implementation is as stable reliable cl...

## Summary

This PR adds a new GO term for **4-phosphoerythronate phosphatase activity** as requested in issue #13 (shadow ticket of geneontology/go-ontology#31118).

### New Term Details

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **ID** | GO:7770035 |
| **Name** | 4-phosphoerythronate phosphatase activity |
| **Namespace** | molecular_function |
| **Definition** | Catalysis of the reaction: 4-phospho-D-erythronate + H2O = D-erythronate + phosphate. |
| **Parent** | GO:0016791 (phosphatase activity) |
| **References** | PMID:27294321, RHEA:86555 |

### Reaction Details

The enzyme catalyzes the hydrolysis of 4-phospho-D-erythronate to produce D-erythronate and inorganic phosphate:

```
4-phospho-D-erythronate + H2O → D-erythronate + phosphate
```

### Gene Products to be Annotated
- Human PGP (UniProt A6NDG6)
- Mouse Pgp (Q8CHP8)  
- Yeast PHO13 (P19881)

### Design Pattern Notes
- Follows the standard phosphatase activity term pattern similar to phosphoglycolate phosphatase activity (GO:0008967)
- Uses simple is_a relationship to parent term (GO:0016791)
- Definition follows standard reaction format

### Notes
- RHEA:86555 is referenced (noted as "not yet public" in original request but included for future linkage)
- The phosphoglycolate phosphatase enzyme (EC 3.1.3.18) is known to catalyze this activity as a metabolite repair function

Closes #13

- [ ] Check parent term relationship is correct
- [ ] Validate definition format matches similar terms

body:
Built a complete CLI tool for transcribing and summarizing YouTube playlists using local AI (NVIDIA NeMo + Ollama), prioritizing privacy and zero recurring costs. Designed as an educational resource for TypeScript developers learning Python.

## Core Implementation

**CLI Interface** (Click + Rich)
- `init` - Setup wizard with SMTP configuration
- `add` - Register playlists with prompt templates
- `list` - Display configured playlists
- `run` - Execute pipeline with progress tracking

**Architecture**
```
┌─── CLI ───┐
│           │
├─ Config   │─── ~/.yt-transcribe/config.yaml
├─ Database │─── SQLite (processed videos)
│           │
├─ Core Services:
│  ├─ Downloader (yt-dlp)
│  ├─ Transcriber (NeMo Parakeet TDT mock)
│  ├─ Summarizer (Ollama)
│  └─ Email (SMTP)
```

**Prompt Templates**
- Built-in: guitar, coding, business
- Custom YAML support with validation
- Playlist-specific AI instructions

**State Management**
- SQLite tracks processed videos to prevent duplicates
- Stores transcriptions and summaries for reference

## Technical Approach

**Type System**
```python
from __future__ import annotations

def get_playlists() -> list[Dict[str, str]]:
    """
    TypeScript Equivalent:
        const getPlaylists = (): Playlist[] => config.playlists
    """
```

**Educational Focus**
Every function includes TypeScript equivalents in docstrings. Uses Python 3.11+ native type syntax (`list[X]` vs `List[X]`).

**Testing**
- 60 unit tests, 58% overall coverage
- Core modules (config, database, templates): 85-100% coverage
- pytest + coverage reporting

**Docker**
- Multi-stage Dockerfile (dev + prod)
- docker-compose with Ollama service
- GPU support ready (NVIDIA Container Toolkit)

**Security**
- CodeQL validated: 0 vulnerabilities
- Explicit GitHub Actions permissions
- No external API dependencies

## Usage Example

```bash
yt-transcribe init
yt-transcribe add --playlist PLxxx --name "Guitar Lessons" --prompt guitar
yt-transcribe run --all --dry-run  # Preview
yt-transcribe run --all            # Execute
```

## Implementation Notes

**Mock Transcription Service**
Placeholder for NVIDIA NeMo Parakeet TDT (600MB model). Real implementation requires `nemo_toolkit` and CUDA. Mock service enables full development/testing without ML dependencies.

**Ollama Integration**
Async client using aiohttp. Expects local Ollama instance at `localhost:11434`. Supports any model (llama2, mistral, etc.).

**Template System**
YAML-based prompts inject domain expertise:
```yaml
name: guitar
system_prompt: |
  Focus on chord progressions, techniques,
  practice exercises, and musical theory.
summary_format: |
  ## Overview
  {summary}
  ## Practice Items
  {actions}
```

**Email Delivery**
Markdown→HTML conversion for rich email formatting. Supports Gmail app passwords and standard SMTP.

The **YouTube Playlist Auto-Transcriber** is a local-first utility that eliminates manual video consumption by providing high-quality, specialized summaries. By leveraging local AI, it ensures effectively zero recurring costs and total data privacy.

### Core Functional Requirements
- **Local Transcription:** Utilize **NVIDIA Parakeet TDT** via the **NVIDIA NeMo** toolkit for 140x–300x real-time transcription.
- **Local Summarization:** Integrate with **Ollama** to tun models and process transcripts locally.
- **Playlist-Specific Prompts:** Allow users to "inject" different system prompts based on the playlist type (e.g., guitar techniques vs. coding patterns).
- **Automated Delivery:** Send formatted Markdown summaries via SMTP (Gmail/iCloud).[6]
- **State Management:** Maintain a local database to ensure videos are only processed once.

### Key User Experience (UX) Goals
- **TypeScript-to-Python Educational Path:** The codebase must use heavy type hinting (`typing` module) and clear docstrings to help a TS developer transition to Python.
- **Robust CLI:** Use the **Click** library for a self-documenting interface with beautiful progress bars using **Rich**.
- **Self-Contained Docker:** A single `docker-compose.yml` should orchestrate the downloader, transcriber, and LLM services.

***

## Technical Architecture

The system follows a "Modular Monolith" approach within a Docker container to minimize setup friction for the user.

| Component | Technology | Role |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Orchestrator** | **Python** 3.11+ | Logic glue, CLI, and state management |
| **Downloader** | **yt-dlp** | Reliable audio extraction from YouTube [7] |
| **Speech-to-Text** | **Parakeet TDT** | 300x real-time transcription with punctuation [2] |
| **Brain** | **Ollama** | Summarization and action item extraction [5] |
| **Infrastructure** | **Docker** | Environment isolation and GHA compatibility [8] |

***

## CLI Interface Specification

The CLI is the primary user interface. It must be "forgiving" by using fuzzy matching for names and providing clear help text for every command.

### 1. Initialization: `yt-transcribe init`
- **Action:** Creates `~/.yt-transcribe/` directory.
- **Onboarding:** Guides the user through setting up SMTP credentials and downloading the 600MB Parakeet model.[9]
- **TS Context:** Similar to `npm init`, but it also handles binary/model dependencies.

### 2. Rule Creation: `yt-transcribe add`
- **Usage:** `add --playlist [ID] --name "Guitar" --prompt guitar`
- **Prompts:** Supports built-in templates (guitar, coding, business) or custom YAML files.
- **Validation:** Immediately verifies the YouTube playlist ID and prompt syntax.

### 3. Execution: `yt-transcribe run`
- **Usage:** `run --id [ID]` or `run --all`
- **UI:** Displays a "Rich" dashboard with a multi-step progress bar (Download → Transcribe → Summarize → Email).
- **Dry Run:** Includes a `--dry-run` flag to show what *would* be processed without spending resources.

***

## Developer Implementation Guide

This section is optimized for a TypeScript developer learning Python patterns while setting up the repo. This is being developed for educational purposes for someone new to these technologies. 

### Python vs. TypeScript Idioms
- **Type Hints:** Use `List[str]` and `Optional[Playlist]` instead of `string[]` or `Playlist | null`.
- **Async:** Use `asyncio` for the Ollama API calls, behaving similarly to `async/await` in Node.js.

author: chalkan3
body:
## Summary

- Add Tailscale as alternative VPN provider to WireGuard
- Implement embedded Tailscale client using tsnet library (no system installation required)
- Add Headscale coordination server deployment via Pulumi
- Implement SOCKS5 proxy for automatic kubectl routing through VPN
- Store Headscale credentials as Pulumi secrets

## New Commands

```bash
# Connect to Tailscale mesh (daemon mode)
sloth-kubernetes vpn connect my-cluster --daemon

# kubectl automatically routes through VPN
sloth-kubernetes kubectl my-cluster get nodes

# Disconnect
sloth-kubernetes vpn disconnect my-cluster
```

## Configuration

```lisp
(network
  (mode "tailscale")
  (tailscale
    (enabled true)
    (namespace "kubernetes")))
```

## Features

- **Embedded Client**: Uses tsnet library, no system-wide Tailscale installation needed
- **SOCKS5 Proxy**: Automatic proxy for kubectl and other tools
- **Daemon Mode**: Run VPN in background with `--daemon`
- **Secrets Management**: Headscale API key stored as Pulumi secret
- **Auto-discovery**: Peers automatically discovered via Headscale

## Test Plan

- [x] Build and test daemon mode
- [x] Test kubectl through VPN

- [x] Update documentation

author: cmungall
body:
## Summary

- Add `validate_title()` method in `SupportingTextValidator` for exact title matching after normalization
- Add `_find_title_fields()` in plugin to discover slots implementing `dcterms:title` or having `slot_uri` dcterms:title
- Add `_validate_title()` in plugin to yield validation results for title mismatches
- Update `_validate_instance()` to validate titles from dedicated title fields, either combined with excerpt validation or standalone

## Title Validation Behavior

Title validation uses **exact matching** (not substring like excerpt) but allows for minor orthographic variation:
- Case insensitivity (`JAK1` matches `jak1`)
- Whitespace normalization (extra spaces collapsed)
- Punctuation differences (`Cell-Signaling` matches `Cell Signaling`)
- Greek letter equivalence (`α-catenin` matches `alpha-catenin`)

## Schema Usage

Slots can be marked for title validation using:
```yaml
slots:
  reference_title:
    implements:
      - dcterms:title
```

Or via `slot_uri`:
```yaml
slots:
  title:
    slot_uri: dcterms:title
```

- [x] All 261 tests pass (`just test`)
- [x] mypy passes

### Motivation

- Provide a runnable, deterministic local implementation of the AWS-style LeetCode pipeline so the repository actually executes end-to-end without AWS credentials.
- Ensure reproducible inputs and outputs by shipping a fixture that mimics the LeetCode API and by avoiding live network dependence by default.

### Motivation
- Fix a `RenderBox` layout crash caused by unbounded constraints introduced by the planning-mode reskin while keeping the new visual (large header + floating cards) intact.
- Ensure scrollable content and animated transitions receive finite constraints so buttons and animations stop producing layout exceptions.
- Avoid changing any business logic, persistence, models, providers or event logging while making layout changes.
- Add a targeted regression test to prevent future regressions on small viewports.

### Description
- Migrate the main planning screen to a single `CustomScrollView` with a header sliver and content provided as `SliverList`/`SliverPadding`, and add `SliverFillRemaining` helpers for loading/empty states to guarantee bounded constraints for scrollable content.
- Replace ad-hoc `ListView` returns with a reusable separated sliver builder so list items and separators are produced inside slivers with correct constraints and spacing.
- Make `AppPrimaryButton` and `AppSecondaryButton` safe for “full width” usage by wrapping that code path in a `LayoutBuilder` and adding a debug `assert` that throws a clear `FlutterError` when the parent does not provide a finite width, while preserving height, pill shape and visual behavior.
- Add a widget-level regression test that renders the main planning screen in a small viewport, performs a scroll, and asserts there are no exceptions and the list is scrollable.

- Restore the terminal UI to the prior stable appearance and behavior after recent changes that introduced a Git Bash–style line editor, a custom cursor, and other visual tweaks that affected the visibility of the typed line.

body:
## Summary

Fixes issue where the exomer complex (GO:0034044) was misdefined. The original definition incorrectly described it as being "involved in exocytosis" when exomer is specifically a vesicle coat complex that mediates selective cargo transport.

### Changes:
- **Definition update**: Changed from "A protein complex that forms a coat structure on vesicles involved in exocytosis of proteins from the trans-Golgi network to the cell surface" to "A vesicle coat complex that mediates selective cargo transport from the trans-Golgi network (TGN) to the plasma membrane"
- **Classification fix**: Changed `is_a` from `GO:0032991` (protein-containing complex) to `GO:0030120` (vesicle coat) - aligning with COPI/COPII vesicle coat classification patterns
- **Component nomenclature**: Updated Saccharomyces component list to include accurate ChAPs (Chs5p-Arf1p-binding proteins) nomenclature
- **Added reference**: PMID:25203211 - key paper establishing exomer as "the only cargo adaptor known to sort proteins at the TGN into secretory vesicles"
- **Added term_tracker_item** linking to original issue

### Scientific rationale:
Research confirms exomer is definitively a vesicle coat complex (PMID:17000877) that mediates selective transport rather than general exocytosis. The new definition better captures its unique role as the only known TGN cargo adaptor.

Closes #10

author: mrjcleaver
body:
This PR offers a devcontainer to create and run your app in GitHub Codespaces.

I'm not sure how far I'll get but it'll save someone else a step if that's the direction they want to go.

Here's Claude's why codespaces slop

# Proposal: Add GitHub Codespaces & Cloud Development Environment Support

## Executive Summary

Supporting cloud development environments (Codespaces, Gitpod, etc.) would significantly **lower barriers to adoption** while **improving security** for both users and the project itself. This is particularly important for personal AI infrastructure that handles sensitive data and API keys.

---

## Benefits to Users

### 1. Security & Trust
- **Sandboxed evaluation**: New users can test your system without risking their primary machine
- **Reduced attack surface**: Compromised dependencies can't access local credentials, SSH keys, or personal files
- **Disposable environments**: Easy to destroy and recreate if something goes wrong
- **Audit trail**: Cloud providers maintain logs of environment activity

### 2. Simplified Onboarding
- **One-click setup**: "Open in Codespaces" button → working environment in 2 minutes
- **No local dependencies**: No Python version conflicts, no PATH issues, no OS-specific bugs
- **Consistent environments**: Everyone runs the same configuration
- **Lower technical barrier**: Non-technical users can evaluate AI infrastructure without installing toolchains

### 3. Cross-Platform Accessibility
- Works from **any device** - Chromebook, iPad, old laptop
- No Mac/WSL requirement - removes platform restrictions
- Access from **anywhere** - coffee shop, library, work machine
- Team collaboration becomes easier

---

## Benefits to the Project

### 1. Increased Adoption
- **Higher conversion rate**: People try before committing to local installation
- **Broader audience**: Reach users who can't/won't install locally
- **Faster feedback loop**: Users can test PRs and new features instantly
- **Community growth**: Lower friction = more contributors

### 2. Better Support Experience
- **Reproducible issues**: "Open in Codespaces" eliminates "works on my machine"
- **Standardized environment**: Reduces support burden from OS/config variations
- **Easier debugging**: Contributors can quickly spin up test environments
- **Reduced setup documentation**: Less time explaining dependencies

### 3. Developer Experience
- **CI/CD alignment**: Test environment matches what users experience
- **Faster contributor onboarding**: New contributors productive in minutes
- **Pre-configured tooling**: Linting, formatting, testing all pre-installed
- **Dev containers as documentation**: `.devcontainer/` folder documents exact setup requirements

### 4. Security Best Practices
- **Demonstrates security consciousness**: Shows you care about user safety
- **Encourages secure patterns**: Users learn to isolate sensitive workloads
- **Secrets management**: Natural place to document proper API key handling
- **Builds trust**: "This project takes security seriously"

---

## Implementation Effort

**Minimal work required:**

```json
// .devcontainer/devcontainer.json (basic example)
{
  "name": "Personal AI Infrastructure",
  "image": "mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:3.11",
  "postCreateCommand": "pip install -r requirements.txt",
  "customizations": {
    "vscode": {
      "extensions": ["ms-python.python"]
    }
  }
}
```

**Time investment**: 1-2 hours initially, minimal maintenance

**Compatibility**: Codespaces, Gitpod, DevPod all use same `.devcontainer/` format

---

## Addressing Common Objections

### "But it requires local file access"
- Codespaces **has persistent storage** - `/workspaces/` persists between sessions
- Can mount secrets as environment variables
- Many personal AI tools work fine in cloud environments

### "Cloud environments cost money"
- GitHub gives **60 hours/month free** for Codespaces
- Users **choose** to use it - doesn't remove local option
- Many users already pay for GitHub Pro (180 hours/month)

### "It's not truly local/private"
- Valid concern for some users - **keep local option**
- But cloud isolation is **more private** than compromised local machine
- Users can self-host with DevPod + their own infrastructure

### "Adds complexity"
- `.devcontainer/` configuration **documents** your setup
- Actually **reduces** complexity for most users
- Maintainer doesn't need to support it heavily - community will help

---

## Competitive Examples

Many similar projects already support this:

- **LangChain**: Full Codespaces support
- **AutoGPT**: Gitpod integration
- **LocalAI**: Dev container configuration
- **Jupyter**: JupyterHub cloud environments

Users increasingly **expect** this option for AI/ML projects.

---

## Proposed Action Items

1. **Phase 1**: Add basic `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` (1 hour) (DONE)

-- WAIT --

3. **Phase 2**: Add "Open in Codespaces" badge to README (5 minutes)
4. **Phase 3**: Document secrets/API key management for cloud environments (30 minutes)
5. **Phase 4**: Gather feedback and iterate

**Total initial investment**: ~2 hours  
**Ongoing maintenance**: Minimal (update with dependency changes)

---

author: frasercl
body:
Review time: small-medium (~20min) (most of the diff is package-lock.json!)

Makes the app smarter about encoding and decoding the `url` query parameter.

## Background

In its simplest form, this query parameter (`vole.allencell.org/viewer?url=...`) contains a single URL to the single image Vol-E should open. But there are multiple ways the user can "open" multiple image URLs at the same time, with corresponding URL param syntax:

- The user can open multiple *scenes*, which they can switch between in a single session, by concatenating multiple URLs with `+`: `example.com/image1.zarr+example.com/image2.zarr`
- Each scene can have multiple *sources*, whose data is combined into a single image, by concatenating multiple URLs with `,`: `example.com/source1.zarr,example.com/source2.zarr+example.com/scene2.zarr`

For a bunch of good reasons these URLs are generally percent-encoded to get rid of special characters. (For example, `http://` becomes `http%3A%2F%2F`.) But it's not clear whether the URLs ought to be encoded individually *before* concatenation or all at once *after* concatenation, or that any given app will be smart enough not to encode it multiple times. The most complex combination I've seen in the wild is scenes that were encoded, concatenated with `+`, then encoded *again*. This *happens* to work currently, but it implies potentially wilder combinations of encodings aren't outside the realm of possibility, and we ought to be prepared for those combinations (regardless of whether they're technically "correct").

## Solution

1. Overhaul how we decode nested lists of URLs in the `url` query parameter, to try to accept arbitrary combinations of encoding and concatenation
2. Add a unit test for 1.
3. Make Vol-E a little bit smarter about not attempting to encode a `url` param that's already encoded
4. This PR also includes a number of version bumps for dev packages, from me trying to get the environment to support the newish `URL.canParse` API for checking URL validity.

body:
## Summary

- Adds `.miserc.toml` - a config file loaded very early in the initialization process, before main config files are parsed
- Primary use case: setting `MISE_ENV` in a config file instead of only via env vars or CLI args
- Settings marked with `rc = true` in settings.toml can be set in .miserc.toml:
  - `env` - the primary use case for setting MISE_ENV
  - `cd` - change directory before loading config
  - `ceiling_paths` (new setting) - where to stop searching for config files
  - `ignored_config_paths` - paths to skip during config discovery
  - `override_config_filenames` - override default config filenames
  - `override_tool_versions_filenames` - override .tool-versions filenames

File locations (in order of precedence):
1. Local: `.miserc.toml` in cwd and ancestors
2. Global: `~/.config/mise/miserc.toml`
3. System: `/etc/mise/miserc.toml`

Precedence: CLI args > env vars > .miserc.toml

Also generates a JSON schema for .miserc.toml at `schema/miserc.json`.

## Test plan

- [ ] New E2E test `test_miserc` verifies:
  - Setting MISE_ENV via .miserc.toml loads correct env-specific config
  - Environment variables override .miserc.toml
  - Subdirectories pick up parent .miserc.toml
- [ ] Existing `test_config_env` test continues to pass
- [ ] Manual testing with `.miserc.toml` files

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Enables early initialization via `.miserc.toml` so settings marked `rc = true` (e.g., `env`, `ceiling_paths`, `ignored_config_paths`, `override_*_filenames`) can influence config discovery before main files load.
> 
> - New `src/config/miserc.rs` to locate/merge `.miserc.toml` from local→global→system; `Cli::run` loads it at startup
> - `env.rs` reads rc settings from miserc as fallback with precedence: CLI > env vars > `.miserc.toml`
> - Codegen: `build.rs` emits `MisercSettings`; `xtasks/render/schema.ts` generates `schema/miserc.json` from `settings.toml` entries with `rc=true`
> - Add `ceiling_paths` setting and mark applicable settings with `rc=true` in `settings.toml`; adjust `schema/mise.json`/`mise-settings.json`

# 온라인 매칭 SSE 변경 PR 코드 리뷰 요약 (업데이트됨)

## 📋 주요 변경사항 (요약)
- SSE 중심 매칭 플로우 도입 및 알림 계약 변경
  - NotificationType.MATCH_FOUND 추가. MATCH_FOUND SSE 이벤트로 매칭 확정/리다이렉트 트리거.
  - MatchingScheduler가 매칭 확정 후 NotificationService로 알림 전송(알림 실패 시 매칭 유지, 알림 단계 예외 격리).
  - 커밋 메시지 및 코드 반영: MatchSessionService와 MatchingScheduler의 duration 단위가 분에서 초(second)로 변경됨.
- SSE/Emitter 단일화 및 안정성 강화
  - SseEmitterRepository: Map<Long, List<SseEmitter>> → Map<Long, SseEmitter> (사용자당 단일 emitter; 멀티탭 동시 수신 동작 변경).
  - NotificationService.subscribe() → save() 변경 및 구독시 20초 heartbeat 스케줄러 등록.
  - NotificationPushService: 단일 SseEmitter 조회/전송으로 변경, IOException/RuntimeException 발생 시 emitter 제거 및 로깅.
  - 프론트(notification-common.js): ensureSseConnected(), heartbeat 및 재연결 로직 추가.
- 매칭 큐/상태 확인 로직 재설계
  - MatchingQueueService: Redis 티켓 의존 제거, user_match_session Redis 키 도입. DB 우선 검사 후 Redis 정리 로직으로 상태 판별 및 정리. cleanupAfterMatched(List<Long>, Long sessionId)로 변경.
  - 신규 메서드: removeQueueByUserId, cleanupUserFromAllQueues, cleanupMatchSession 등 추가.
- 거리별 레이팅 API 및 응답 확장
  - DistanceRatingController/DistanceRatingService, DistanceRatingResDto(currentRating, currentTier) 추가. 엔드포인트: GET /api/rating/distance?distanceType=
  - MatchWaitingParticipantDto에 tier 필드 추가; MatchSessionService에서 참가자별 tier 포함 응답 생성 → 응답 스펙 변경(클라이언트 동기화 필요).
- 인증·예외 처리 강화
  - JwtFilter: TokenProvider/RedisTemplate 주입, shouldNotFilterAsyncDispatch()/shouldNotFilterErrorDispatch()를 false로 설정(ASYNC/ERROR dispatch에서도 필터 동작), Redis 블랙리스트 체크 추가.
  - JwtAccessDeniedHandler / JwtAuthenticationEntryPoint: response.isCommitted() 체크로 중복 응답 방지.
  - GlobalExceptionHandler: 시그니처에 HttpServletRequest 추가, AsyncRequestNotUsableException 전용 핸들러 추가, Accept: text/event-stream 요청에 대해 204 처리(500 방지).

## ✅ API/스펙 점검 및 영향
- DistanceRatingController 응답: ApiResponse<DistanceRatingResDto>(currentRating, currentTier), HTTP 200 — 스펙 일치(문서화 필요).
- Match 관련 응답에 participant DTO에 tier 필드 추가 → 응답 스펙(필드명·타입·null 허용 여부) 문서화 및 클라이언트 마이그레이션 필요.
- Jwt 관련 에러 핸들링은 기존 JSON 구조를 유지하되 response.isCommitted() 분기 때문에 일부 상황에서 응답이 생략될 수 있음 — 모니터링/클라이언트 처리 영향 검토 필요.
- 프론트엔드 전역 API(window.ensureSseConnected 등) 추가로 글로벌 네임스페이스 영향 고려 필요.

## ⚠️ 호환성·운영 영향
- 백엔드/프론트 동시 배포 권장: MATCH_FOUND 이벤트 계약 및 tier 필드 변경으로 클라이언트 의존성 존재.
- SseEmitter 단일화로 멀티탭·멀티디바이스 동시 수신 행태 변경(최근 연결 우선) — 기존 UX 요구사항과 일치하는지 확인 필요.
- JwtFilter가 ASYNC/ERROR dispatch에서도 동작하도록 변경됨 → 비동기 경로 성능 영향 및 인증 흐름 영향 검증 필요.
- NotificationService의 구독별 ScheduledExecutorService 생성 구조는 구독 해제 시 스케줄러 종료 보장이 필요함(스레드 누수 우려).
- MatchingQueueService의 Redis/DB 혼합 검사에서 race condition 가능성 존재 — Redisson 락 및 Lua 스크립트와의 상호작용 확인 필요.

## 🔍 주요 코드 검토 포인트 (우선 검증 권장)
1. DistanceRatingService 트랜잭션 경계
   - getUserDistanceRating()가 readOnly 트랜잭션에서 createNewRating(REQUIRES_NEW)를 호출하는 구조인지, readOnly 설정이 새 엔티티 생성에 영향이 없는지 확인.
2. NotificationService heartbeat 스케줄러 관리
   - 구독(또는 save) 시 생성되는 ScheduledExecutorService의 수명 관리(구독 취소 시 shutdown) 및 스레드풀 재사용 고려.
3. MatchingQueueService 동시성/일관성
   - DB 우선 검사 → Redis 정리 흐름의 race condition 검증. ADD_QUEUE_ATOMIC_SCRIPT, Redisson 락 범위·원자성 확인.
4. JwtFilter의 ASYNC/ERROR dispatch 영향
   - 필터 재진입, 중복 인증/캐싱 이슈, 성능 영향 및 예외 처리 경로 검증.
5. SseEmitterRepository.save()의 기존 emitter.complete() 정책
   - 기존 연결 강제 종료가 클라이언트 재연결 UX에 미치는 영향과 서버 로그/모니터링 영향 확인.
6. GlobalExceptionHandler의 SSE(204) 처리
   - SSE 요청에 204를 반환하는 흐름이 클라이언트 재연결/에러 핸들링 기대 동작과 일치하는지 확인.
7. 프론트 전역 네임스페이스 영향
   - notification-common.js, online-match.js가 window 전역에 다수 함수/상태 추가 — 다른 스크립트와의 충돌 여부 점검.

## 코드 컨벤션·설계 준수 및 테스트 권장
- ApiResponse 패턴, @AuthenticationPrincipal 사용 등 팀 컨벤션은 전반적으로 준수됨.
- 변경된 컴포넌트(JwtFilter, MatchingQueueService, NotificationService 등) 복잡도 증가 — 단위/통합/부하 테스트 및 문서화(특히 SSE 이벤트 사양) 필요.
- 프론트 대규모 변경(online-match.js/CSS/템플릿) → E2E/브라우저 테스트, 접근성·반응형 검증 권장.

## 권장 작업(체크리스트)
- [ ] DistanceRatingService 트랜잭션 경계(특히 readOnly vs createNewRating(REQUIRES_NEW)) 재검토 및 보증.
- [ ] NotificationService heartbeat 스케줄러 리소스 관리(구독 해제 시 스케줄러 종료 보장 또는 스레드풀 재사용).
- [ ] MatchingQueueService의 Redis/DB 동기화·락 범위·Lua 스크립트 상호작용 검증(경합 상황 테스트).
- [ ] SseEmitter 단일화 의도 확인(멀티탭 UX 요구사항) 및 문서화.
- [ ] JwtFilter ASYNC/ERROR 적용 영향(성능·인증 시나리오) 검증.
- [ ] GlobalExceptionHandler의 SSE(204) 처리 방식이 클라이언트 재연결/에러 UX와 일치하는지 확인.
- [ ] 프론트/백엔드 배포 동기화: MATCH_FOUND 이벤트 계약 및 응답에 추가된 tier 필드 문서화.

author: copilot
body:
HubSpot's CRM v4 Associations API was returning 400 error because `associationTypeId` was being passed as string `"contact_to_listing"` instead of numeric ID. HubSpot does not accept string association type names.

### Changes

- **`src/lib/hubspot.ts`**: Remove body from PUT request to use HubSpot's default association
- **Documentation**: Remove obsolete `HUBSPOT_CONTACT_LISTING_ASSOCIATION_TYPE` env var from `HUBSPOT_INTEGRATION.md` and `REQUEST_INFO_INTEGRATION.md`

### Before (broken)
```typescript
const associationResponse = await fetch(url, {
  method: 'PUT',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  },
  body: JSON.stringify([{
    associationCategory: 'USER_DEFINED',
    associationTypeId: 'contact_to_listing', // ❌ string not allowed
  }]),
});
```

### After (fixed)
```typescript
const associationResponse = await fetch(url, {
  method: 'PUT',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
  },
  // No body = use HubSpot's default association
});
```

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ✅ Current state (this is great)
> 
> Your result:
> 
> {
>   contactSubmitted: true,
>   marketingConsentSet: true,
>   listingFound: true,
>   associationCreated: false
> }
> 
> 
> Means:
> 
> ✅ Forms API works
> 
> ✅ Contact created/updated
> 
> ✅ Marketing consent set
> 
> ✅ Listing lookup by external_listing_id works
> 
> ❌ Association call failed
> 
> So the only thing broken now is the association payload.
> 
> 🔴 The exact error (decoded)
> 
> HubSpot says:
> 
> Invalid input JSON on line 1, column 60:
> Cannot deserialize value of type `int`
> from String "contact_to_listing"
> 
> What this means in plain English
> 
> You are sending this (or equivalent):
> 
> {
>   "associationType": "contact_to_listing"
> }
> 
> 
> But HubSpot expects:
> 
> {
>   "associationTypeId": 123
> }
> 
> 
> 👉 Association types are numeric IDs, not string names.
> 
> HubSpot does not accept:
> 
> "contact_to_listing"
> 
> "listing_to_contact"
> 
> "CONTACT_TO_LISTING"
> 
> Even though those names exist conceptually.
> 
> ✅ How HubSpot associations actually work
> 
> In the CRM v4 Associations API, you must supply:
> 
> fromObjectType
> 
> toObjectType
> 
> numeric associationTypeId
> 
> There is no automatic resolution from string → ID.
> 
> The correct fix (2 options)
> ✅ Option A (Recommended): Use the default association (simplest)
> 
> For standard object ↔ standard object associations (Contacts ↔ Listings), HubSpot provides a default association type.
> 
> You do not need to specify a custom type at all.
> 
> Correct request (recommended)
> await fetch(
>   `https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v4/objects/contacts/${contactId}/associations/listings/${listingId}`,
>   {
>     method: "PUT",
>     headers: {
>       Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN}`,
>       "Content-Type": "application/json",
>     },
>   }
> );
> 
> 
> ✅ No body
> ✅ No associationType
> ✅ Uses HubSpot’s default association
> 
> This is what you want unless you explicitly created custom association labels.
> 
> Why your current call fails
> 
> You are likely doing something like:
> 
> body: JSON.stringify({
>   associationType: "contact_to_listing"
> })
> 
> 
> HubSpot tries to parse "contact_to_listing" as an integer → 💥 400.
> 
> ✅ What to change right now (do this)
> 🔧 Fix your association helper
> 
> Before (wrong):
> 
> body: JSON.stringify({
>   associationType: "contact_to_listing"
> })
> 
> 
> After (correct, recommended):
> 
> // no body at all
> 
> 
> Or, if your helper requires a body, remove the field entirely.
> 
> Expected result after this fix
> 
> On the next form submit, you should see:
> 
> {
>   success: true,
>   details: {
>     contactSubmitted: true,
>     marketingConsentSet: true,
>     listingFound: true,
>     associationCreated: true
>   }
> }
> 
> 
> And in HubSpot:
> 
> Contact ↔ Listing association visible
> 
> Contact appears under “Associated contacts” on the Listing
> 
> Listing appears under “Associated listings” on the Contact
> 
> TL;DR (final)
> 
> ❌ HubSpot does NOT accept string association names
> 
> ✅ Associations require numeric IDs
> 
> ✅ Default association needs no body at all
> 
> Remove associationType: "contact_to_listing"
> 
> Redeploy
> 
> You’re done


</details>

body:
## Summary

Fixes #5532

- Sanitizes filenames containing path separators (e.g., `payslips/red/genuine/uuid.pdf`) by using `os.path.basename()` before passing to `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile()`
- Adds unit test to verify the fix

## Root Cause

When users upload files with filenames containing path separators, the full path was passed as the `suffix` parameter to `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile()`, causing a `FileNotFoundError` because the temp file system tried to create nested directories that don't exist.

## Test plan

- [x] Added unit test `test_file_schema_decode_with_path_separator_in_filename`
- [x] Verified test fails without the fix
- [x] Verified test passes with the fix
- [x] Ran existing IO unit tests to ensure no regressions (76 tests pass)

body:
This pull request expands the support for PyOD-based unsupervised anomaly detection models in the WSADBench framework. It updates the `PyOD.py` baseline to improve model loading, initialization, and fitting logic, and adds configuration files for several PyOD models, making them easier to use and configure. Additionally, it enhances the model class path mapping in `run_experiment.py` to ensure all supported PyOD models are recognized and routed correctly.

**PyOD Model Integration and Improvements:**

- Updated `WSADBench/baseline/PyOD.py` to:
  - Import additional PyOD models (`DIF`, `ALAD`, `LUNAR`) and add them to the model dictionary if available. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b8236509aadaf8210bf7677fccae3773726ccfcc9932a74f5b40def71ae7e200L28-R39) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b8236509aadaf8210bf7677fccae3773726ccfcc9932a74f5b40def71ae7e200L50-R63)
  - Refine model initialization and fitting logic, including improved handling for `DeepSVDD`, and a new `normal_only` option for fitting only on normal samples for certain models. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b8236509aadaf8210bf7677fccae3773726ccfcc9932a74f5b40def71ae7e200L174-R190) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b8236509aadaf8210bf7677fccae3773726ccfcc9932a74f5b40def71ae7e200L205-R222) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b8236509aadaf8210bf7677fccae3773726ccfcc9932a74f5b40def71ae7e200L281-R316)

**Configuration and Usability Enhancements:**

- Added new YAML configuration files for various PyOD models, including `AutoEncoder`, `CBLOF`, `DeepSVVD`, `ECOD`, `LOF`, `LUNAR`, `PCA`, and `VAE`, to the `WSADBench/model_configs/tabular/` directory. These files standardize and simplify model setup. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3c5e92dcc6226174cf200f468cfe3a8cd1314e9a6d2282772b77d3064740346bR1-R13) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b7b96f7b9fafdea89e48b3e846280472d68b0275a3d153779b563b55ce10acd9R1-R13) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5be7dc519aa6229ba611f0f6155e80e20a9e4108b6c3fab92ff8978a52c6bb1fR1-R13) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-6814526c7f9b013be4a392146e455494440d8b5c34fff975a940d0b6e079705bR1-R13) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-61adfc87fe6293d69a9a71c486aaad95463a730d37981112fd971d371fc0f61cR1-R13) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-35c29de30c9e0f80e6e2dfbf155eb022bc73dddd467266603d5a0ded33bbe127R1-R13) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-cf7e261e3f998aa89a1dfdcb0506f87642e051410cfe79825c38d0c047cbaac4R1-R13) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-fe5a19e6b3d3e8a2378bdccd77a844713e190cf830210b9fada4ce8791615798R1-R13)

author: brucehoff
body:
Add a Realm object which has an id, a name and a list of identity providers (IdPs).
An IdP is either Synapse or it is an OAuthProvider.
No two realms can share an identity provider (so when you authenticate via an IdP you are unambiguously authenticating to a realm).
Add a realm id field to UserGroup (FK to realm).
Add a PrincipalRealm relation for the default principals for each realm.  Each record has a realm ID, a principal ID, and a type (anonymous, authenticated, pubic, admin).

Admin services for creating and deleting realms. (Note, there is no update service at this time.)
Non-admin services to list the realm IDs, get a realm by its ID and get a realm's default principals by its ID.

author: shyukahn
body:
This PR implements the instantiation and dynamic semantics of for statements. Additionally, test cases with for statements using the v1model architecture are added.

1. Instantiation semantics
    
    Rules for the relation `Stmt_inst` are added to implement for statements as well as break and continue statements.
    
2. Dynamic semantics
    
    The following relations are added to implement the dynamic semantics of for statements:
    
    - `ForUpdateStmt_eval` / `ForUpdateStmts_eval`
    - `ForInitStmt_eval` / `ForInitStmts_eval`
    - `ForThreeClauseLoop_eval`
    - `ForCollectionExpr_eval`
    - `ForInLoop_eval`
    
    The rules for 3-clause for statements are implemented in `rulegroup Stmt_eval/forStatementIR-three-clause`. After executing the init statements, `ForThreeClauseLoop_eval` handles the actual loop execution, which includes checking the condition and executing the loop body and the update statements.
    
    The rules for for-in statements are implemented in `rulegroup Stmt_eval/forStatementIR-in`. `ForCollectionExpr_eval` evaluates the collection expression and `$get_values_from_collection` is a helper function that gets the list of values from the collection. `ForInLoop_eval` handles the loop execution by iterating over the values.
    
    To handle break and continue statements, `forBreakResult` and `forContinueResult` are added to `statementResult`.
    
3. Testcases
    
    Example test cases are added to a temporary folder `temp-for-testdata`. Each case consists of a p4 file and an stf file.
    
4. Minor fixes
    - `rule Call_eval/block-copyin-cont-ActionBody-exit`: If evaluating an action body results in `EXIT`, calling the action should also result in `EXIT`.
    - `rule Call_eval/tableApplyMethodCallee-exit`: This is a new rule to handle when calling a table apply method results in `EXIT`.

Let n be the number of nodes in the tree.

Time complexity: O(n)

We visit every node exactly once during the Depth First Search traversal. At each node, we perform constant time operations (addition and comparison).

Space complexity: O(n)

The space complexity is determined by the recursion stack depth. In the worst case (a skewed tree), the recursion can go O(n) deep. In a balanced tree, the height is O(logn).

author: caffeinebounce
body:
## Summary

Adds `DisplayField`, `DisplayFieldGroup`, and `ProfileSection` components to `@caffeinebounce/ui` for building profile and detail views.

Closes #35, #37

## Background

These patterns are duplicated across multiple files in Compass:
- `DisplayField` in CohortProfile.tsx, CompanyProfile.tsx (~80 lines)
- `InfoField` in UserProfile.tsx, AdminCompanyProfile.tsx (~90 lines)  
- `ProfileSection` in CohortProfile.tsx, CompanyProfile.tsx (~150 lines)

## Components Added

### DisplayField

A label/value display component with support for:
- Icons (via `icon` prop or `platform` for social icons)
- Links (with external link indicator)
- Custom placeholders
- Multiline values

```tsx
// Basic usage
<DisplayField label="Company Name" value={company.name} />

// With icon
<DisplayField label="Email" value={user.email} icon={Mail} />

// As link with social platform icon
<DisplayField 
  label="LinkedIn" 
  value={linkedinUrl} 
  href={linkedinUrl} 
  platform="linkedin" 
/>
```

### DisplayFieldGroup

A grid wrapper for organizing multiple DisplayField components:

```tsx
<DisplayFieldGroup columns={2}>
  <DisplayField label="Name" value={user.name} />
  <DisplayField label="Email" value={user.email} />
</DisplayFieldGroup>
```

### ProfileSection

A section wrapper for profile pages with:
- Card and simple variants
- Edit/Save/Cancel action buttons
- Collapsible sections
- Icon support

```tsx
// Editable section
<ProfileSection
  title="Company Details"
  icon={Building}
  isEditing={isEditing}
  onEdit={() => setIsEditing(true)}
  onCancel={() => setIsEditing(false)}
  onSave={handleSave}
  isSaving={isSaving}
>
  {isEditing ? <EditForm /> : <DisplayContent />}
</ProfileSection>

// Collapsible section
<ProfileSection title="Advanced Settings" collapsible defaultCollapsed>
  <SettingsForm />
</ProfileSection>
```

## Estimated Impact

- **Lines saved**: ~200+ lines across 5+ files
- **Files affected**: 5+ in Compass
- **Risk level**: Low (presentational components)

## Checklist

- [x] Components build successfully
- [x] Types exported from package index
- [x] JSDoc documentation added
- [ ] Compass updated to use shared components (follow-up PR)

<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 2.6.3
   ```
   ==================

- Fixed a high-severity security issue where decompression-bomb safeguards of
  the streaming API were bypassed when HTTP redirects were followed.
  (`GHSA-38jv-5279-wg99 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-38jv-5279-wg99>`__)
- Started treating ``Retry-After`` times greater than 6 hours as 6 hours by
  default. (`3743 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3743>`__)
- Fixed ``urllib3.connection.VerifiedHTTPSConnection`` on Emscripten.
  (`3752 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3752>`__)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.6.2
   ```
   ==================

- Fixed ``HTTPResponse.read_chunked()`` to properly handle leftover data in
  the decoder's buffer when reading compressed chunked responses.
  (`3734 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3734>`__)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.6.1
   ```
   ==================

- Restore previously removed ``HTTPResponse.getheaders()`` and
  ``HTTPResponse.getheader()`` methods.
  (`3731 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3731>`__)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.6.0
   ```
   ==================

Security
--------

- Fixed a security issue where streaming API could improperly handle highly
  compressed HTTP content ("decompression bombs") leading to excessive resource
  consumption even when a small amount of data was requested. Reading small
  chunks of compressed data is safer and much more efficient now.
  (`GHSA-2xpw-w6gg-jr37 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-2xpw-w6gg-jr37>`__)
- Fixed a security issue where an attacker could compose an HTTP response with
  virtually unlimited links in the ``Content-Encoding`` header, potentially
  leading to a denial of service (DoS) attack by exhausting system resources
  during decoding. The number of allowed chained encodings is now limited to 5.
  (`GHSA-gm62-xv2j-4w53 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-gm62-xv2j-4w53>`__)

.. caution::
  - If urllib3 is not installed with the optional `urllib3[brotli]` extra, but
    your environment contains a Brotli/brotlicffi/brotlipy package anyway, make
    sure to upgrade it to at least Brotli 1.2.0 or brotlicffi 1.2.0.0 to
    benefit from the security fixes and avoid warnings. Prefer using
    `urllib3[brotli]` to install a compatible Brotli package automatically.

  - If you use custom decompressors, please make sure to update them to
    respect the changed API of ``urllib3.response.ContentDecoder``.


Features
--------

- Enabled retrieval, deletion, and membership testing in ``HTTPHeaderDict`` using bytes keys. (`3653 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3653>`__)
- Added host and port information to string representations of ``HTTPConnection``. (`3666 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3666>`__)
- Added support for Python 3.14 free-threading builds explicitly. (`3696 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3696>`__)


Removals
--------

- Removed the ``HTTPResponse.getheaders()`` method in favor of ``HTTPResponse.headers``.
  Removed the ``HTTPResponse.getheader(name, default)`` method in favor of ``HTTPResponse.headers.get(name, default)``. (`3622 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3622>`__)


Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed redirect handling in ``urllib3.PoolManager`` when an integer is passed
  for the retries parameter. (`3649 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3649>`__)
- Fixed ``HTTPConnectionPool`` when used in Emscripten with no explicit port. (`3664 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3664>`__)
- Fixed handling of ``SSLKEYLOGFILE`` with expandable variables. (`3700 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3700>`__)


Misc
----

- Changed the ``zstd`` extra to install ``backports.zstd`` instead of ``zstandard`` on Python 3.13 and before. (`3693 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3693>`__)
- Improved the performance of content decoding by optimizing ``BytesQueueBuffer`` class. (`3710 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3710>`__)
- Allowed building the urllib3 package with newer setuptools-scm v9.x. (`3652 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3652>`__)
- Ensured successful urllib3 builds by setting Hatchling requirement to >= 1.27.0. (`3638 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3638>`__)

Features

现有前端界面缺乏现代化的设计感和视觉美感，需要进行全面的UI重构以提供更专业、更友好的用户体验。同时，系统需要支持浏览器端的音频播放功能，以便用户能够直接在浏览器中听到Sonic的语音回复。

## 解决方案

### 1. 前端UI重构 (index.html)

#### 视觉设计改进
- **现代化布局**: 采用渐变背景 (紫蓝渐变)，提升整体视觉效果
- **卡片式设计**: 使用圆角卡片和柔和阴影，增强层次感
- **响应式布局**: 优化flex布局，确保在不同屏幕尺寸下的良好表现
- **专业配色**: 主色调为紫色系 (#667eea, #764ba2)，提升品牌形象

#### 界面元素优化
- **消息气泡重设计**: 
  - System消息: 浅灰色背景，小字体
  - AI消息: 蓝色渐变气泡，左对齐
  - 用户消息: 紫色渐变气泡，右对齐
  - 语音图标: 改用emoji 🎤，增加可读性

- **控制面板改进**:
  - 更清晰的按钮分组和视觉层次
  - 圆形按钮设计，提升交互性
  - 状态指示器优化，使用图标和颜色编码

- **场景面板优化**:
  - 清晰的场景卡片设计
  - 图标支持 (药物、注射器、心脏emoji)
  - hover效果和选中状态视觉反馈

### 2. 浏览器音频播放功能

#### 核心功能实现
- **Web Audio API集成**:
  - 创建AudioContext管理音频播放
  - 实现音频队列管理，支持流式播放
  - 处理音频解码和播放控制

- **TTS API端点** (`main.py`):
  - 新增 `/voice/tts` REST API端点
  - 接收文本和系统提示，返回base64编码的音频
  - 异步处理音频生成，提升性能

- **音频播放功能**:
  ```javascript
  playTextAsSpeech(text, systemPrompt)  // 播放文本转语音
  playAudioFromBase64(base64Audio)      // 播放base64音频
  playNextAudioChunk()                  // 队列管理
  ```

#### AWS Bedrock Nova Sonic集成
- 利用现有的 `voice_handler.process_text_to_speech()` 方法
- 支持流式音频生成和传输
- 错误处理和状态管理

### 3. 后端增强 (main.py)

#### 新增TTS端点
```python
@app.route('/voice/tts', methods=['POST'])
def text_to_speech():
    # 文本转语音处理
    # 返回base64编码的音频数据
```

#### WebSocket音频流优化
- 改进语音流处理逻辑
- 增强错误处理机制
- 优化音频chunk传输

## 技术实现细节

### 前端技术栈
- **Web Audio API**: 浏览器原生音频处理
- **Fetch API**: RESTful API调用
- **CSS3**: 渐变、动画、圆角、阴影
- **JavaScript ES6+**: async/await、Promise、箭头函数

### 后端技术栈
- **Flask**: Web框架
- **asyncio**: 异步音频处理
- **base64**: 音频数据编码
- **AWS Bedrock**: Nova Sonic TTS服务

### 关键技术点
1. **音频格式处理**: 支持PCM格式音频的解码和播放
2. **异步流处理**: 使用asyncio处理音频流生成
3. **队列管理**: 实现音频chunk的队列播放机制
4. **状态管理**: 跟踪播放状态，防止并发问题

## 测试建议

### 基础功能测试
1. ✅ **UI显示测试**
   - 打开应用，检查新UI是否正确渲染
   - 验证渐变背景和卡片样式
   - 测试消息气泡的显示效果

2. ✅ **场景选择测试**
   - 点击不同的场景卡片
   - 验证选中状态的视觉反馈
   - 确认场景切换功能正常

3. ✅ **音频播放测试**
   - 发送文本消息给AI
   - 验证是否能听到Sonic的语音回复
   - 检查音频播放状态指示器

### 进阶功能测试
4. ✅ **语音交互测试**
   - 点击"开始语音"按钮
   - 说话后验证语音识别和回复
   - 测试双向语音对话流程

5. ✅ **错误处理测试**
   - 断开网络连接，测试错误提示
   - 测试音频播放失败的处理
   - 验证系统消息的显示

6. ✅ **响应式测试**
   - 调整浏览器窗口大小
   - 验证在不同屏幕尺寸下的显示
   - 测试移动端兼容性

## 实现清单

- ✅ 前端UI完全重构，采用现代化设计
- ✅ 实现浏览器端音频播放功能
- ✅ 集成AWS Bedrock Nova Sonic TTS
- ✅ 新增 `/voice/tts` REST API端点
- ✅ 优化音频流处理和队列管理
- ✅ 改进错误处理和状态管理
- ✅ 保持与现有Flask后端的完全兼容
- ✅ 保持与voice_handler工具的集成

## 兼容性说明

- ✅ 完全兼容现有Flask后端 (main.py)
- ✅ 无缝集成voice_handler工具
- ✅ 支持现有的WebSocket语音流功能
- ✅ 向后兼容所有现有API端点
- ✅ 保留所有原有功能特性

## 视觉改进

本次重构显著改善了用户界面的视觉美感和专业性：
- 从简单的白色背景升级为渐变设计
- 增强了视觉层次和信息架构
- 提升了品牌专业形象
- 改善了用户体验和交互流畅度

## Background

Dynamic imports (`await import()`) were being used in tsup.config.ts files to read package.json for version information. This PR converts them to static imports for consistency and cleaner code.

## Summary

Converted all 32 tsup.config.ts files across packages to use static imports instead of dynamic imports for reading package.json:

**Before:**
```typescript
define: {
  __PACKAGE_VERSION__: JSON.stringify(
    (await import('./package.json', { with: { type: 'json' } })).default.version,
  ),
},
```

**After:**
```typescript
import pkg from './package.json' with { type: 'json' };
// ...
define: {
  __PACKAGE_VERSION__: JSON.stringify(pkg.version),
},

### Motivation
- Resolve the fatal "OrbitControls is not defined" error by switching to module imports so the demo reliably starts.
- Replace the flat metamer array with a recursive tree (Metamer) so branches can have multiple children and produce realistic branching.
- Add pipe-model tapering so branch diameters scale from downstream leaf area for more realistic geometry.
- Provide a lab-style diagnostics UI (T/R balance, C/N gauge, NSC) to observe physiological state during simulation.

### Description
- Replaced `web/index.html` with a new FSPM Lab layout that uses an `importmap` to load `three` and `three/addons/` modules and imports `OrbitControls` as an ES module.
- Implemented an in-page `Metamer` class, growth logic (`simulateDay`), recursive thickness computation (`getTotalLeafArea` / `updateThickness`), and tree visualization built from stacked `THREE.CylinderGeometry` segments with bud meshes.
- Wired UI controls (`btn-step`, `btn-auto`, `btn-reset`) and a diagnostics dashboard that updates T/R balance, C/N gauge, and NSC values based on simulation state.
- Removed the previous UMD/`sketch.js` coupling and switched to an embedded module script that handles initialization, animation, and scene updates.

### Testing
- Launched a local static server with `python -m http.server 8000` and used a Playwright script to open `http://127.0.0.1:8000/index.html` and capture a screenshot, which succeeded and produced an artifact.

body:
Implements CSV generation for AFL player SuperCoach statistics across seasons 2023-2025, fetching data from footywire.com and saving CSV files directly to the file system.

## Implementation

- **`scripts/generateCSVs.js`**: Node.js script that fetches SuperCoach scores across all rounds (up to 24 per season), calculates per-player averages, generates CSV files with columns: Player Name, Games Played, Total Score, Average SuperCoach Score
- **Output**: CSV files saved to `dataOutput/afl_supercoach_{year}.csv` in the project root
- **Input validation**: Year/round parameters validated to prevent injection
- **Constants extraction**: `REQUEST_DELAY_MS`, `MAX_AFL_ROUNDS`, `AVAILABLE_YEARS` for maintainability
- **CSV compliance**: RFC 4180 compliant quote escaping for proper CSV format

## Usage

```bash
cd apps/sc-builder
npm install
npm run generate-csvs
```

This generates three CSV files in the `dataOutput/` folder:
- `afl_supercoach_2023.csv`
- `afl_supercoach_2024.csv`
- `afl_supercoach_2025.csv`

## Technical Details

- Uses `jsdom` for HTML parsing in Node.js environment
- 500ms delay between requests to be respectful to external servers
- Proper error handling and progress logging throughout execution
- Generated CSV files are excluded from git via `.gitignore`

## Data Source

- **FootyWire**: `https://www.footywire.com/afl/footy/supercoach_round?year={year}&round={round}&p=&s=T` - SuperCoach scores

The script runs standalone in Node.js, fetches data from external sources, processes it, and saves CSV files directly to the file system without any UI interaction.

PR #35750: [se] Add support for custom kernel argument packing via template specialization

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/35750

Main changes are in `xla/stream_executor/kernel_args.h`.

* Consistently use `KernelArgPacking` to pack custom arguments to device kernels. 
* Add a test for overriding default packing mechanism via template specializations.
* Rename `KernelArgument` to `KernelArg` for consistency with other types
* Rename `KernelArgPackingRelocation::Type` to `Kind` for a bit more consistency with other parts of XLA, and because `Type` is used in many places to reference a C++ type
* Simplify how `KernelArgsPackedArray` stores POD arguments and remove a bunch of templates.

This change is needed to be able to pass NCCL device communicators to custom kernels without leaking NCCL headers from public XLA headers, and instead hiding kernel argument packing inside NCCL collectives library.

- The Jest test setup previously injected environment-specific plugin stubs (small React/JXS shims) via `registerPluginSandboxLibraries`, but those are not needed for the library-level tests and couple the test harness to UI-specific endowments.

- Kept `markHardenedEnvironmentForTesting()` in `packages/skaff-lib/tests/setup-env.ts` to provide the test-safe harden/polyfill used in Jest instead of calling SES `lockdown()`. 
- No other API or production code was modified; this is strictly a test setup cleanup. 
- The change is limited to `packages/skaff-lib/tests/setup-env.ts` (14 deletions).

author: sosukesuzuki
body:
## Summary

Replace VirtualQuery-based stack bounds calculation with `GetCurrentThreadStackLimits` on Windows when `BUN_JSC_ADDITIONS` is enabled.

## Problem

The previous VirtualQuery-based implementation assumes a specific 3-layer stack structure (uncommitted → guard → committed) which can fail when:

- Guard pages are consumed by another thread ([BrokenGuardPage issue](https://github.com/chaelim/BrokenGuardPage))
- Security software scans process memory and triggers guard page exceptions
- The stack is fully committed (no uncommitted region)
- Embedded application scenarios ([Ruby Bug #11438](https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/11438))

When these assumptions are violated, `StackBounds` returns incorrect values, causing `preCommitStackMemory` to crash with STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW (0xC00000FD).

## Solution

`GetCurrentThreadStackLimits` returns OS-maintained stack limits that are:

- Independent of guard page state
- Independent of VirtualQuery results
- Accurate regardless of stack memory layout

## Code Change

```cpp
StackBounds StackBounds::currentThreadStackBoundsInternal()
{
    ULONG_PTR lowLimit = 0;
    ULONG_PTR highLimit = 0;
    GetCurrentThreadStackLimits(&lowLimit, &highLimit);

    void* origin = reinterpret_cast<void*>(highLimit);
    void* bound = reinterpret_cast<void*>(lowLimit);
    return StackBounds { origin, bound };
}
```

## References

- https://github.com/chaelim/BrokenGuardPage
- https://devblogs.microsoft.com/oldnewthing/20220203-00/?p=106215
- https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/11438

`run  [--reuse-test (optional)pipeline-id --disable-fail-fast --skip-test --stage-list "A10-PyTorch-1, xxx" --gpu-type "A30, H100_PCIe" --test-backend "pytorch, cpp" --add-multi-gpu-test --only-multi-gpu-test --disable-multi-gpu-test --post-merge --extra-stage "H100_PCIe-TensorRT-Post-Merge-1, xxx" --detailed-log --debug(experimental)]`

Launch build/test pipelines. All previously running jobs will be killed.

`--reuse-test (optional)pipeline-id ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Allow the new pipeline to reuse build artifacts and skip successful test stages from a specified pipeline or the last pipeline if no pipeline-id is indicated. If the Git commit ID has changed, this option will be always ignored. The DEFAULT behavior of the bot is to reuse build artifacts and successful test results from the last pipeline.

`--disable-reuse-test ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Explicitly prevent the pipeline from reusing build artifacts and skipping successful test stages from a previous pipeline. Ensure that all builds and tests are run regardless of previous successes.

`--disable-fail-fast ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Disable fail fast on build/tests/infra failures.

`--skip-test ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Skip all test stages, but still run build stages, package stages and sanity check stages. Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub check status.

`--stage-list "A10-PyTorch-1, xxx"` *(OPTIONAL)* : Only run the specified test stages. Examples: "A10-PyTorch-1, xxx". Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub check status.

`--gpu-type "A30, H100_PCIe"` *(OPTIONAL)* : Only run the test stages on the specified GPU types. Examples: "A30, H100_PCIe". Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub check status.

`--test-backend "pytorch, cpp"` *(OPTIONAL)* : Skip test stages which don't match the specified backends. Only support [pytorch, cpp, tensorrt, triton]. Examples: "pytorch, cpp" (does not run test stages with tensorrt or triton backend). Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub pipeline status.

`--only-multi-gpu-test ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Only run the multi-GPU tests. Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub check status.

`--disable-multi-gpu-test ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Disable the multi-GPU tests. Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub check status.

`--add-multi-gpu-test ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Force run the multi-GPU tests in addition to running L0 pre-merge pipeline.

`--post-merge ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Run the L0 post-merge pipeline instead of the ordinary L0 pre-merge pipeline.

`--extra-stage "H100_PCIe-TensorRT-Post-Merge-1, xxx"` *(OPTIONAL)* : Run the ordinary L0 pre-merge pipeline and specified test stages. Examples: --extra-stage "H100_PCIe-TensorRT-Post-Merge-1, xxx".

`--detailed-log ` *(OPTIONAL)* : Enable flushing out all logs to the Jenkins console. This will significantly increase the log volume and may slow down the job.

`--debug ` *(OPTIONAL)* : **Experimental feature**. Enable access to the CI container for debugging purpose. Note: Specify exactly one stage in the `stage-list` parameter to access the appropriate container environment. Note: Does **NOT** update GitHub check status.

For guidance on mapping tests to stage names, see `docs/source/reference/ci-overview.md`
and the `scripts/test_to_stage_mapping.py` helper.

### kill

`kill  `

Kill all running builds associated with pull request.

### skip

`skip --comment COMMENT `

Skip testing for latest commit on pull request. `--comment "Reason for skipping build/test"` is required. IMPORTANT NOTE: This is dangerous since lack of user care and validation can cause top of tree to break.

### reuse-pipeline

`reuse-pipeline `

Reuse a previous pipeline to validate current commit. This action will also kill all currently running builds associated with the pull request. IMPORTANT NOTE: This is dangerous since lack of user care and validation can cause top of tree to break.

author: realronaldrump
body:
### Motivation
- Error logs showed `pymongo.errors.InvalidOperation: Cannot use MongoClient after close` when API handlers reused collection objects bound to a closed client.
- Holding collection instances from `db_manager.db[...]` can retain stale client handles across event-loop or connection changes.
- The intent is to ensure collections are resolved against the current `DatabaseManager` client to avoid intermittent DB errors.

### Description
- Import `CollectionProxy` from `db` and replace direct `db_manager.db["trips"]` and `db_manager.db["app_settings"]` with `CollectionProxy("trips")` and `CollectionProxy("app_settings")` in `admin_api.py`.
- This makes collection resolution lazy so calls always use the active MongoDB client managed by `DatabaseManager`.
- No other API behavior or endpoints were changed.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.

author: necony286
body:
### Motivation
- The Next.js production build failed because Playwright modules were being bundled into server code, causing module resolution errors for `chromium-bidi`, `electron`, and other assets.
- Bundling Playwright pulls in binary and web assets that Next.js/webpack cannot process during server compilation and leads to build-time failures.
- The change prevents these runtime-heavy packages from being inlined into the server bundle so the build can complete successfully.

### Description
- Added `serverExternalPackages: ['playwright', 'playwright-core']` to `next.config.js` to mark Playwright packages as external for server builds.
- The update ensures Next.js will not attempt to bundle `playwright` and `playwright-core` into server-side output.
- No other source files were modified.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run after this change.
- The change is targeted at resolving the previously observed `next build` webpack errors related to Playwright module resolution.

author: ajeesh24
body:
Root Cause Analysis:
- Browser/S3 conflicts when loading same presigned URL in dual audio elements
- "Buffer metadata failed to load" errors occurred because primary and buffer elements were trying to access identical S3 URLs simultaneously

Critical Fix:
- Get fresh presigned URL specifically for buffer element during transitions
- Use different cache-busting parameters (?buffer= vs ?retry=) to avoid conflicts
- Refresh URLs on each retry attempt to prevent stale URL issues

Technical Details:
- Call audifyApi.getAudioPresignedUrl() to get dedicated buffer URL
- Fallback to cache-busted original URL if fresh URL fetch fails
- Each retry attempt gets completely fresh presigned URL

This should resolve the "Buffer metadata failed to load" errors and enable seamless audio transitions to work properly with growing audio files.

body:
## Summary

Adds a GitHub Actions release workflow that builds and publishes nudge binaries to GitHub Releases. The workflow is patterned after the [hurry release workflow](https://github.com/attunehq/hurry/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml), including macOS code signing and notarization.

**Supported platforms (same as hurry):**
- macOS: x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-apple-darwin (signed and notarized)
- Linux GNU: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu  
- Linux musl: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
- Windows: x86_64-pc-windows-gnu

**Trigger:** Push of `v*` tags (e.g., `v0.1.0`) or manual workflow dispatch with dry run option.

**Output:** Draft GitHub release with tarballs for each platform and SHA256 checksums.

## Updates since last revision

1. Added a build script (`packages/nudge/build.rs`) that extracts the version from git tags using `git describe --always --tags`. This ensures the binary version matches the release tag (e.g., tagging `v0.1.0` produces `nudge v0.1.0` in `--version` output). Patterned after the hurry build script.

2. Added macOS code signing and notarization steps using Apple Developer credentials. Requires these repository secrets: `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_BASE64`, `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_ID`, `APPLE_TEAM_ID`, `APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD`.

**Previously tested:** Pushed test tag `v0.0.1-test`, verified all 7 platform builds succeeded, downloaded the musl binary, and confirmed `nudge --version` outputs `nudge v0.0.1-test`. Test tag and draft release were cleaned up. (Note: this was before macOS signing was added.)

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Verify macOS signing works**: Push a test tag (e.g., `v0.0.2-test`) and confirm the macOS builds complete successfully with signing and notarization. Download a macOS binary and verify it runs without Gatekeeper warnings.
- [ ] **Verify secrets are configured correctly**: Confirm all 5 Apple secrets are set in the repository settings.
- [ ] **Verify Rust edition 2024 compatibility**: The nudge `Cargo.toml` uses `edition = "2024"` but the workflow installs `stable` toolchain. Confirm stable Rust supports edition 2024, or update to use nightly.
- [ ] **Verify version output on a real release**: After merging, tag a real release (e.g., `v0.1.0`) and confirm the published binary shows the correct version.

### Notes

macOS signing requires the Apple Developer secrets to be configured in the repository. The workflow will fail on macOS builds if these secrets are missing or incorrect.
